hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap as needs outpace available money
hero.teaser: Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall, and the gap between what the county needs and what it can afford could shape how residents get around for decades.
hero.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next 20 years, a gap that could determine how residents travel for decades to come.

The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements through 2050, but only $701 million is currently available. That means the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Nearly all of the available funding comes from state and federal sources, with only $10 million coming from local revenue. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August and outlines transportation needs across roads, transit, aviation, freight, and other infrastructure categories.

Among the most pressing unfunded needs are nine roads the county identified as requiring widening as traffic grows. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, money that is not currently available, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. Without funding for these widening projects, the county will be unable to address growing congestion on these corridors.

State Road 710 stands out as among the county's highest priorities and has been the subject of repeated safety concerns. About $300 million in projects are planned for the corridor, reflecting the urgent need for improvements on this route. The massive funding shortfall highlights the challenge facing Martin County as it tries to balance transportation demands with limited financial resources over the coming decades.

cards.headline: Severe weather brings waterspouts, lightning strikes and fires to Treasure Coast
cards.body:
Friday's severe weather left a trail of impacts across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County, with waterspouts, lightning strikes and multiple fires reported throughout the region.

Multiple videos sent to the WPTV newsroom from Sebastian showed a large waterspout passing over the Indian River Lagoon Friday afternoon. In Port St. Lucie, weather spotters captured video of heavy rain moving through the area, with resident Merry Moore O'Rourke reporting over 3 inches in her rain gauge. Moore O'Rourke described the storm's intensity: "All of a sudden, it got black. The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen." She added, "I mean it was radical. I mean it was a little scary."

The severe weather stretched to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. In Port St. Lucie, Lucie County Fire District crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that lightning ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. Fire crews also responded to a house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue during the evening storm. WPTV radar picked up significant lightning in the area at the time, though Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

Port St. Lucie saw particularly significant lightning activity throughout the day as the storms moved through the region. The waterspouts, lightning strikes and fires from Friday's severe weather serve as a reminder of nature's unpredictable power during Florida's storm season.

cards.headline: Waterspout crosses Indian River Lagoon near Sebastian as severe weather strikes region
cards.body:
A large waterspout passed over the Indian River Lagoon near Sebastian Friday afternoon as severe weather battered the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Multiple videos sent to the WPTV newsroom captured the waterspout moving through the area as the storm system left a trail of impacts across the region.

The severe weather brought heavy rain to Port St. Lucie, where weather spotters documented the downpour moving through the area. Merry Moore O'Rourke reported her rain gauge caught over 3 inches of rain. She described the frightening conditions as the storm intensified. "All of a sudden, it got black. The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen," Moore O'Rourke said. She summed up the experience by calling it radical and a little scary, reflecting what many across the region felt as the storms moved through.

Lightning strikes sparked multiple fires in Port St. Lucie as significant electrical activity accompanied the severe weather. Lucie County Fire District crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. Fire crews also responded to a house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue during the evening. Radar detected a significant amount of lightning in the area at the time of the storm. Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause of the house fire, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

The severe weather extended beyond Port St. Lucie into Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. The storm system stretched across the entire region, demonstrating nature's unpredictable power. From waterspouts over the Indian River Lagoon to dangerous lightning strikes that sparked fires and injured residents, Friday's severe weather impacted communities throughout the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. The combination of heavy rainfall, powerful winds, intense lightning activity and waterspouts made for dangerous conditions that residents described as some of the most dramatic weather they had witnessed in the area.

cards.headline: JetBlue ending Vero Beach to JFK route in September due to low demand
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He explained that JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said. However, he noted that the Boston route is performing well, saying "Boston is seeing great demand."

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot at success. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He emphasized the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying "It's easy. It's close." Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. Dambeck said the door is not closed for the route to return in the future. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

cards.headline: Lightning strikes ignite brush fire and house fire in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: Friday's severe weather brought heavy lightning activity to Port St. Lucie, sparking fires that required emergency response.
cards.body:
Friday's severe weather brought heavy impacts to Port St. Lucie, including lightning-sparked fires and intense rainfall that alarmed residents across the area.

Lucie County Fire District said crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. The severe weather moved through Port St. Lucie on Friday afternoon, with weather spotters capturing video of heavy rain. Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge caught over 3 inches. She described the sudden intensity of the storm and how conditions changed rapidly.

"All of a sudden, it got black. The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen," Moore O'Rourke said. The severe weather extended beyond Port St. Lucie, stretching all the way to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. In Sebastian, weather spotters sent video showing a large waterspout passing over the Indian River Lagoon Friday afternoon. Port St. Lucie experienced significant lightning activity throughout the storm system.

At the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue, fire crews responded to an evening house fire. At the time of the storm, radar picked up a significant amount of lightning in the area. Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate. The timing of the house fire coincided with the peak of the severe weather moving through the region.

Moore O'Rourke summed up what many across the region felt as the storms moved through. "I mean it was radical. I mean it was, it was a little scary," Moore O'Rourke said. From waterspouts to lightning strikes and fires, Friday's severe weather served as a reminder of nature's unpredictable power across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County.

cards.headline: Boca Raton man arrested for soliciting videos from minor in Boynton Beach
cards.teaser: Maximiliano Buitrago, 51, was arrested after allegedly responding to an undercover post and asking a 14-year-old for videos.
cards.body:
A 51-year-old man was arrested for soliciting videos from a minor, according to Boynton Beach police. Maximiliano Buitrago of Boca Raton was arrested on charges of solicitation to commit human trafficking and unlawful use of a two-way communication device, after asking a 14-year-old for videos. Buitrago allegedly responded to a Craigslist post offering summer babysitting services that undercover detectives from the Human Exploitation Unit had placed, asking, "Are you trying to make cash any other way? What else can you do?"

Investigators say Buitrago repeatedly acknowledged that the girl was 14, and offered her money for videos that he claimed would be viewed by clients overseas. On July 16, Buitrago arranged a meetup with the girl at a Boynton Beach park, where he was taken into custody. Police searched his vehicle and discovered cards stating, "Make money on TikTok with pics and short videos," along with an offer to "get paid cash." Buitrago confessed to investigators and is being held at Palm Beach County jail. Boynton Beach police believe there could be more victims, and ask anyone who might have received that card or messaged with Buitrago to contact BBPD Detective Joseph at 561-742-6158.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County woman wins $5 million on $20 scratch-off ticket
cards.teaser: Maria Duran of St. Lucie County claimed a $5 million top prize from a scratch-off game purchased at a Fort Pierce store.
cards.body: Maria Duran, 57, claimed a $5 million top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6, Florida Lottery officials announced Friday. Duran chose to receive her winnings as a one-time, lump-sum payment of $3,262,138. She purchased her winning ticket from PK 2 Quick Mart, located at 4101 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce. The game's overall odds of winning are 1-in-2.90, but the chance of winning $5 million is 1-in-4,018,135.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach VA Healthcare System holds resource fair at Big Dog Ranch Rescue in Loxahatchee
cards.teaser: The VA hosted a resource fair for veterans on Friday, offering enrollment assistance and health care services at the Loxahatchee facility.
cards.body:
The West Palm Beach VA Healthcare System hosted a resource fair for veterans on Friday at Big Dog Ranch Rescue in Loxahatchee. VA representatives assisted veterans with eligibility and health care enrollment, VA health care programs and claims support. A mobile medical unit was on site to address basic medical needs and allowed veterans to complete an initial primary care appointment on the spot and get into the VA system. Richard "Buzz" Bryan, director of community relations and community engagement for the West Palm Beach VA Healthcare System, said the event focused on reaching veterans who have not yet connected with VA services. Bryan, a combat veteran himself, said he did not utilize VA services for years and wants other veterans to learn from his experience.

Big Dog Ranch Rescue was on site to provide information about its service dog training program, animal adoption opportunities and additional veteran-focused services. Bryan said the organization's veteran service program is outstanding and there is not a better place to get a service animal. Veterans who were unable to attend can call the West Palm Beach VA Healthcare System at (561) 422-8387 or access enrollment and health care resources online.

cards.headline: Boynton Beach Fire Rescue saves dog that fell into raw sewage lift station
cards.teaser: A specialized confined space rescue operation was launched Thursday after a dog fell roughly 10 to 12 feet into a lift station containing raw sewage.
cards.body:
A dog fell roughly 10 to 12 feet into a lift station holding about 2 feet of raw sewage Thursday, prompting a specialized confined space rescue by Boynton Beach Fire Rescue Department. Squad 6 crews arrived and assessed the scene before upgrading the incident to a Special Operations confined space rescue, the department said. Firefighters developed a rescue plan and had Firefighter Ramirez properly rigged and ready to enter the lift station.

From the time he went on air, Firefighter Ramirez rescued the dog and safely exited the lift station in just 4 minutes, the department said. Once above ground, crews decontaminated the dog and gave it oxygen before turning it over to Animal Control. Animal Control successfully reunited the dog with its owner, according to a Facebook post from the department.

hero.headline: Britain's Josh Kerr breaks mile world record with 3:42.66 time in London
hero.teaser: Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 at a Diamond League event in London on Saturday, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's 27-year-old world record of 3:43.13 set in 1999.
hero.body:
Josh Kerr broke the mile world record on Saturday in London, running 3:42.66 at a Diamond League event and shattering Hicham El Guerrouj's previous mark of 3:43.13 set in 1999. The 27-year-old Great Britain runner made no secret that he was targeting the long-standing record. Earlier in the week, he revealed he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial. His sponsor, Brooks, dubbed the effort "Project 222," referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds. American Yared Nuguse finished second in the race in 3:45.69.

Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, he starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles and set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. Kerr's record-setting run came during the Diamond League, an established international circuit of professional track and field events, meaning the performance was conducted under standard race conditions and is eligible for official world-record status.

cards.headline: Argentina defeats England 2-1 in World Cup semifinal with late comeback goals
cards.teaser: Argentina rallied from a 1-0 deficit with goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez in the final minutes to beat England 2-1 and advance to the World Cup final against Spain.
cards.body:
Argentina scored two goals in the final five minutes to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinal on Wednesday. Enzo Fernandez equalized in the 85th minute with a shot from outside the box after receiving a pass from Lionel Messi. Lautaro Martinez headed in the winner two minutes into stoppage time from a Messi cross.

England had taken the lead through Anthony Gordon in the 55th minute and appeared headed to the final until Argentina's late rally. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves and Alexis Mac Allister hit the post as Argentina pressed for an equalizer. The loss marked the third time England has lost in the World Cup semifinals after previous defeats to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018.

Argentina will face Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The defending champions have repeatedly fought back from difficult positions throughout the tournament. Coach Lionel Scaloni said the team's collectiveness and brotherhood allowed them to keep fighting until the end.

cards.headline: MLB restricts dugout iPad use to prevent teams from using AI for in-game decisions
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible starting Wednesday night to prevent teams from using artificial intelligence to make decisions about substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game choices.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night when the second half of the season began. The league restricted the tablets to prevent them from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The custom tab had expanded the use of dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches, according to a June 11 memo from MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword. The memo was sent to general managers, assistant general managers and video coordinators.

The tablets still have access to video and league-provided data. A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Instituting the prohibition beginning with the second half of the season was intended to provide clubs that had relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead time to make any necessary adjustments, Sword wrote. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Photographer captured images of Messi bathing Yamal as baby in 2007, now they meet in World Cup final
cards.teaser: Joan Monfort photographed teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in 2007 for a charity calendar. The two will face each other Sunday when Argentina plays Spain in the World Cup final.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing a baby boy named Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate in the photo shoot. The infant was paired with Messi, who would become the greatest of all time, according to Monfort. A tearful Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble, and Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

Monfort, 58, who works as a freelance photojournalist for the Associated Press, had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship. The photo went viral then, but interest has skyrocketed ahead of Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without credit or compensation. Monfort said his heart is split between the two players. He has an everlasting love for Messi, whom he considers the best player of all time, but said Yamal has broken the mold and represents a new, diverse Spain thanks to his parents from Morocco and Equatorial Guinea. Monfort is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey.

cards.headline: Security ramped up for World Cup final in New Jersey with Secret Service perimeter for Trump attendance
cards.teaser: Federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies have implemented a security plan two years in the making for Sunday's World Cup final, with enhanced measures including a Secret Service perimeter because President Trump will attend.
cards.body:
A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. For Sunday's match, FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there's anything that needs to be done from a threat perspective.

The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security. When Trump attended an NBA Finals game last month in New York, police shut down several city blocks around the arena and fans were forced to wait in extra-long lines to go through enhanced security.

cards.headline: Flip City gymnasts from Treasure Coast earn national top 15 finish, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.body:
Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month, qualifying them for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine competed as a team and came close to a perfect score during the competition. The team achieved a 9.9 score at nationals, which Head Coach Candice Lazuka said was very close to the difficult perfect 10 mark.

The three gymnasts each came to the sport through different paths. Rose-Daris said it wasn't really about gymnastics but rather the fact that she knew how to do a cartwheel. Supan was inspired by all the gymnasts she saw on YouTube and how amazing they are and how fun it looks. Rine said she loves gymnastics because she learns new things. Lazuka described the season as really good, with the team competing locally, traveling, and advancing to states and regionals. Rose-Daris said it's going to be really fun going to an entire different part of the world for the Junior Olympics. Supan described the qualification as happy and exciting at the same time. Rine said her focus heading into the competition is getting first place on floors.

hero.headline: Boca Raton synagogue invites Treasure Coast families to join summer volunteer program
hero.body:
Families looking for ways to give back this summer can take part in the TLC Program at B'nai Torah Congregation in Boca Raton, where volunteers help with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. The program is led by Summer Faerman and is part of B'nai Torah Congregation's broader effort to connect people of all ages with mitzvah opportunities or meaningful good deeds. Organizers say the TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed and has helped make service a central part of synagogue life since 2012.

B'nai Torah Congregation describes the TLC Program as a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. The congregation says the program focuses on hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations, special needs and other community concerns. Participants can volunteer in a variety of ways, including making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology.

Organizers say the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation. The goal is to show service as something practical, welcoming and easy to begin. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida.

B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap as needs outpace available money
hero.teaser: Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall, and the gap between what the county needs and what it can afford could shape how residents get around for decades.
hero.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next 20 years, a gap that could determine how residents travel for decades to come.

The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements through 2050, but only $701 million is currently available. That means the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Nearly all of the available funding comes from state and federal sources, with only $10 million coming from local revenue. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August and outlines transportation needs across roads, transit, aviation, freight, and other infrastructure categories.

Among the most pressing unfunded needs are nine roads the county identified as requiring widening as traffic grows. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, money that is not currently available, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. Without funding for these widening projects, the county will be unable to address growing congestion on these corridors.

State Road 710 stands out as among the county's highest priorities and has been the subject of repeated safety concerns. About $300 million in projects are planned for the corridor, reflecting the urgent need for improvements on this route. The massive funding shortfall highlights the challenge facing Martin County as it tries to balance transportation demands with limited financial resources over the coming decades.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce woman wins $5 million from $20 scratch-off ticket
hero.body:
Florida Lottery officials announced Friday that Maria Duran, 57, of St. Lucie County claimed a $5 million top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6. Duran chose to receive her winnings as a one-time, lump-sum payment of $3,262,138.

Duran purchased her winning ticket from PK 2 Quick Mart, located at 4101 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce. The ticket cost $20.

The game's overall odds of winning are 1-in-2.90. The chance of winning the $5 million top prize playing this game is 1-in-4,018,135.

Florida Lottery officials released the announcement Friday detailing the jackpot win that occurred earlier this year.

hero.headline: Waterspout crosses Indian River Lagoon near Sebastian as severe weather strikes region
hero.body:
A large waterspout passed over the Indian River Lagoon near Sebastian Friday afternoon as severe weather battered the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Multiple videos sent to the WPTV newsroom captured the waterspout moving through the area as the storm system left a trail of impacts across the region.

The severe weather brought heavy rain to Port St. Lucie, where weather spotters documented the downpour moving through the area. Merry Moore O'Rourke reported her rain gauge caught over 3 inches of rain. She described the frightening conditions as the storm intensified. "All of a sudden, it got black. The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen," Moore O'Rourke said. She summed up the experience by calling it radical and a little scary, reflecting what many across the region felt as the storms moved through.

Lightning strikes sparked multiple fires in Port St. Lucie as significant electrical activity accompanied the severe weather. Lucie County Fire District crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. Fire crews also responded to a house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue during the evening. Radar detected a significant amount of lightning in the area at the time of the storm. Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause of the house fire, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

The severe weather extended beyond Port St. Lucie into Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. The storm system stretched across the entire region, demonstrating nature's unpredictable power. From waterspouts over the Indian River Lagoon to dangerous lightning strikes that sparked fires and injured residents, Friday's severe weather impacted communities throughout the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. The combination of heavy rainfall, powerful winds, intense lightning activity and waterspouts made for dangerous conditions that residents described as some of the most dramatic weather they had witnessed in the area.
